about_text.value: In the dying hours of an epoch, Civilization—the personified voice of an entire age—has been murdered in the sealed archives where influence is measured and traded. The Counter Archivist's mirror-ledger shows a single transaction that broke everything: trust transferred to death itself. As The Mediator, you must navigate competing factions vying for control over what remains of institutional power. Each suspect claims their alibi was verified by the archive; each holds secrets about influence traded before the killing stroke. But in a system where power is conserved and evidence can be counter-balanced, discovering who killed Civilization may not prevent the real tragedy: whoever controls the ledger after you decide becomes the new architect of death.

characters.name: The Mediator
characters.description: A broker of uneasy settlements who tracks public sentiment and timing windows.

characters.name: The Institutional Steward
characters.description: The Institutional Steward is pulled into the murder inquiry by motive, alibi, or fear.

characters.name: The Counter Archivist
characters.description: A patient anti-institution that keeps a mirror-ledger of power: it cancels quiet influence with evidence, leaks, and paradox-proof memory.

characters.name: The Shadow Broker
characters.description: The Shadow Broker is pulled into the murder inquiry by motive, alibi, or fear.

characters.name: The Memory Keeper

text_script.value: Civilization lies in the influence chamber, their form dissolved into scattered ledger fragments. The Counter Archivist stands over them, hands stained with iridescent power residue—the visible signature of murdered institutional weight. They turn to you without surprise, as if they were expecting this moment. 'The final transaction is always messy,' they say. Someone has already begun erasing evidence from the primary records.
"Show me your ledger before it's destroyed."
The Archivist hesitates, then produces a mirror tablet showing a suspicious balance transfer occurring seconds before death.
The Archivist hesitates, then produces a mirror tablet showing a suspicious balance transfer occurring seconds before death.
"Who else was here when you found the body?"
They list three names but omit one—the Institutional Steward was present and left before anyone noticed.
They list three names but omit one—the Institutional Steward was present and left before anyone noticed.
"The power residue on your hands—explain that."
'This isn't murder residue—it's what remains when influence dies.' They're hiding something by over-explaining.
'This isn't murder residue—it's what remains when influence dies.' They're hiding something by over-explaining.

The chamber where influence is traded shows signs of struggle—shattered measurement crystals, spilled power reserves. A partial transaction log remains readable: someone attempted to transfer massive institutional weight immediately before Civilization's death. The transaction failed, incomplete. Whatever was being moved during that moment became the murder weapon.
"Examine the failed transaction for source and destination."
The source is ambiguous but the destination points to a shell entity controlled by the Shadow Broker.
The source is ambiguous but the destination points to a shell entity controlled by the Shadow Broker.
"Search for traces of who initiated the transfer."
Digital forensics reveal institutional access—the Institutional Steward's clearance level.
Digital forensics reveal institutional access—the Institutional Steward's clearance level.
"Check if anyone else had authorization to move that weight."
Four others did—the Shadow Broker, the Memory Keeper, and two dead accounts.
Four others did—the Shadow Broker, the Memory Keeper, and two dead accounts.

The Counter Archivist's private sanctum is a maze of mirror ledgers—each recording the inverse of official transactions. They watch you closely, knowing what you seek. 'I cancel quiet influence,' they say. 'But someone killed the loudest voice in our system.' Their own ledger shows evidence tampering occurred after the murder.
"Show me your mirror record of the murder hour."
They comply reluctantly, revealing a transaction that contradicts their alibi slightly—but not conclusively.
They comply reluctantly, revealing a transaction that contradicts their alibi slightly—but not conclusively.
"Who tampered with evidence after the death?"
'Someone who knew how our ledger works.' They show you a clearance signature—the Memory Keeper.
'Someone who knew how our ledger works.' They show you a clearance signature—the Memory Keeper.
"Are you innocent or just covering your tracks?"
'I keep balance. I don't kill—balance requires all parties.' Their answer is evasive but not a confession.
'I keep balance. I don't kill—balance requires all parties.' Their answer is evasive but not a confession.

The Steward sits at Civilization's old desk as if they belong there already. They offer you tea from a cup that once belonged to the dead. 'Civilization was failing,' they say casually. 'Someone had to make difficult choices for institutional survival.' Their office contains documents about a planned succession.
"I found your clearance on the failed transfer log."
'Many have that level of access. Why single me out?' They're defensive but prepared with excuses.
'Many have that level of access. Why single me out?' They're defensive but prepared with excuses.
"What was this 'planned succession'?"
'Civilization had to yield power eventually. We were negotiating a peaceful transition.' They're lying.
'Civilization had to yield power eventually. We were negotiating a peaceful transition.' They're lying.
"Were you in the archive when they died?"
They confirm being there but claim to have left early—omitting that witnesses placed them near the body.
They confirm being there but claim to have left early—omitting that witnesses placed them near the body.

Hidden beneath layers of institutional blind spots, the Shadow Broker deals in information that never made it to official ledgers. They laugh at your investigation. 'Civilization was already dead—the body just took a moment to catch up.' Their walls display evidence they sold intelligence about the murder window before it happened.
"Who did you sell information to?"
'Information has many buyers. But I can tell you who asked the right questions at the wrong time.' Points to Steward.
'Information has many buyers. But I can tell you who asked the right questions at the wrong time.' Points to Steward.
"Show me what you know about the failed transfer."
They reveal a third party attempted to intercept the transaction mid-flight—the Memory Keeper.
They reveal a third party attempted to intercept the transaction mid-flight—the Memory Keeper.
"What's your real motive in all this?"
'Chaos is profitable, but I prefer chaos with direction.' They planned to profit regardless of who won.
'Chaos is profitable, but I prefer chaos with direction.' They planned to profit regardless of who won.

Civilization studies the room where The Counter Archivist's absence has become the central fact. The Mediator offers a polished memory, but the adaptation's older themes keep leaking through the furniture, gestures, and alibis. The player must decide whether to preserve the obvious murder frame, follow a symbolic clue, or pressure the witness until the scene exposes its second story.
"Play me those recordings you mentioned earlier."
They reveal a conversation between the Steward and an unknown party discussing 'necessary transitions.'
They reveal a conversation between the Steward and an unknown party discussing 'necessary transitions.'
"Why did you tamper with evidence after the murder?"
'To protect what truly matters—truth that doesn't serve power.' They hid something important.
'To protect what truly matters—truth that doesn't serve power.' They hid something important.
"Who did you try to intercept the failed transfer from?"
'I was trying to save what I could of Civilization's influence before it scattered.' Innocent motive.
'I was trying to save what I could of Civilization's influence before it scattered.' Innocent motive.

The player must decide whether to preserve the obvious murder frame, follow a symbolic clue, or pressure the witness until the scene exposes its second story.
"Describe whoever left the archive first."
'Tall figure in institutional colors—could be the Steward or one of their subordinates.'
'Tall figure in institutional colors—could be the Steward or one of their subordinates.'
"What was this influence crystal?"
'A weapon that can dissolve institutional weight on contact—lethal if aimed at someone like Civilization.'
'A weapon that can dissolve institutional weight on contact—lethal if aimed at someone like Civilization.'
"Did anyone enter the archive before or after them?"
'Several came and went—but only one left carrying something suspicious.'
'Several came and went—but only one left carrying something suspicious.'

Back at the Counter Archivist's domain, you find a hidden ledger entry that contradicts everything recorded officially. Someone planted evidence to make it appear as if the Counter Archivist killed Civilization in an act of institutional cleansing. But this frame-up has errors—it was done by someone who knows the system too well.
"Who would know our ledger systems this thoroughly?"
'Only those with top clearance—primarily the Steward and...' They trail off, unwilling to name you directly.
'Only those with top clearance—primarily the Steward and...' They trail off, unwilling to name you directly.
"Why would someone frame you for this?"
'Because I'm the obvious suspect—the anti-institution that keeps mirror records.' They're being set up.
'Because I'm the obvious suspect—the anti-institution that keeps mirror records.' They're being set up.
"Show me exactly where the frame-up was planted."
They point to a transaction timestamp that aligns with the Steward's claimed alibi—proving it false.
They point to a transaction timestamp that aligns with the Steward's claimed alibi—proving it false.

The Mediator offers a polished memory, but the adaptation's older themes keep leaking through the furniture, gestures, and alibis. The player must decide whether to preserve the obvious murder frame, follow a symbolic clue, or pressure the witness until the scene exposes its second story.
"Confront them with this evidence immediately."
The Steward admits nothing but says: 'Progress requires sacrifice.' Their denial is barely a denial.
The Steward admits nothing but says: 'Progress requires sacrifice.' Their denial is barely a denial.
"Investigate who else knew about this plan."
Several Institutional subordinates were informed—the Shadow Broker was tipped off but not involved.
Several Institutional subordinates were informed—the Shadow Broker was tipped off but not involved.
"Find proof of when the plan was initiated."
The plan predates Civilization's visible decline—this was long-term institutionalicide.
The plan predates Civilization's visible decline—this was long-term institutionalicide.

You have enough evidence to accuse someone—but who? The Counter Archivist was framed. The Shadow Broker profited but didn't kill. The Memory Keeper tried to save what they could. The Institutional Steward planned the dissolution and had motive, means, opportunity. But there's something deeper here you might still be missing.
"Confront the Steward with everything you've found."
They admit to planning but claim Civilization was already dying—they just 'helped it along.'
They admit to planning but claim Civilization was already dying—they just 'helped it along.'
"Investigate whether there's another layer to this murder."
Digging deeper reveals Civilization may have been planning their own exit—the Steward just forced the timing.
Digging deeper reveals Civilization may have been planning their own exit—the Steward just forced the timing.
"Check if someone else used the chaos to commit the real murder."
The evidence becomes murky—multiple parties manipulated events, making true guilt diffuse.
The evidence becomes murky—multiple parties manipulated events, making true guilt diffuse.

In the deepest archive—a place not even the Counter Archivist fully tracks—you find Civilization's own final records. They knew they were failing and had prepared a controlled dissolution. But the Steward discovered this and hijacked the plan, turning planned retirement into murder to seize control of what remained.
"Conclude with the Steward as the killer—evidence supports it."
The institutional structure accepts your conclusion—the Steward is removed but the system remains corrupted.
The institutional structure accepts your conclusion—the Steward is removed but the system remains corrupted.
"Acknowledge Civilization's role in their own death."
'They were already dead,' says the Archivist. 'The Steward just signed the death certificate.'
'They were already dead,' says the Archivist. 'The Steward just signed the death certificate.'
"Question whether any single party is truly guilty here."
This line of thinking leads somewhere dangerous—somewhere the investigation wasn't meant to go.
This line of thinking leads somewhere dangerous—somewhere the investigation wasn't meant to go.

Press the official alibi.
The witness yields a useful detail, but suspicion hardens around the obvious suspect.

Study the symbolic clue.
The room's motifs connect across scenes, opening a less obvious route through the mystery.

Protect the frightened witness.
Trust rises, danger falls briefly, and the culprit loses control of the social script.
Trust rises, danger falls briefly, and the culprit loses control of the social script.

You accuse the Institutional Steward based on evidence of planning and motive. The system accepts this verdict—the Steward is removed from power, replaced by someone equally institutional but less ambitious. Civilization remains dead, their influence scattered among those who profit from their absence. You solved the murder but failed to understand it.

You fall for the frame-up and accuse the Counter Archivist. They're removed from power, their mirror ledgers destroyed as dangerous instruments of counter-influence. The Institutional Steward quietly consolidates control over what remains. You didn't just fail to solve the murder—you enabled its true purpose.

You accuse the Shadow Broker based on their profit motive and information trading. They're arrested but before you can extract real answers, they die in custody—conveniently. The truth dies with them, leaving the Institutional Steward free to continue consolidating power under your cover.

You pressure the Memory Keeper too hard and they break, confessing to something they didn't do—protecting their archive from your investigation. The real killer walks free while an innocent party takes the fall. The records you sought are destroyed along with them.

By questioning whether any single party is guilty, you discover the truth: the system itself murdered Civilization through slow institutional erosion long before the Steward delivered the killing blow. You—The Mediator—are part of that system. Every choice you made in this investigation reinforced the structures that killed them. The real murder wasn't an event; it was a process you helped facilitate by mediating between those who wanted to survive at Civilization's expense.
